title: Best Lawn Mowers UK
short: Cordless, electric, petrol and manual lawn mowers compared by cutting width, battery life and power, for lawns of every size.
intro: The right lawn mower depends heavily on your lawn's size and how much cable-free convenience you want to pay for. This guide compares mowers tested by Expert Reviews on the same two lawns, one small and flat, one large and uneven, to judge handling, blockages and mulching.

products.name: LM2236E-SP
products.best_for: Large gardens that want petrol-rivalling power without the fumes
products.key_spec: 56V 10Ah battery, self-propelled, 55cm cutting width, cuts up to 2,000m2 per charge
products.summary: Expert Reviews' favourite mower, with the most powerful lawn mower battery it's tested giving torque that easily rivals a petrol model, plus a 1-hour full recharge. It's self-propelled with variable speeds and handles bumps and inclines well, though at 31kg and with a £469 battery, it's a serious investment.
pros: Best mower battery Expert Reviews has tested
Torque rivals petrol mowers
Self-propelled with variable speeds
Fast 1-hour recharge
cons: Very expensive, largely due to the battery

products.name: RMA 235
products.best_for: Small to medium gardens on a budget
products.summary: Expert Reviews called this a 'veritable bargain', lightweight, easy to use and relatively quiet at 75dBA, mowing well even on damp grass with an excellent 77-minute runtime per charge. The grass collector is bulky and fiddly to empty, and the handle doesn't fold flat for storage.
pros: Excellent value, especially if you already own an AK20 battery
Lightweight and quiet
Excellent runtime per charge
cons: Handle doesn't fold flat for storage

products.name: Nitro WG737E
products.best_for: Medium to large lawns, including rougher or overgrown grass
products.summary: Gives petrol-rivalling cutting power with cordless convenience, handling seriously long, stringy and unruly grass with only occasional jamming in Expert Reviews' testing. Construction feels sturdy and semi-pro, though it's a relatively big, heavy mower and runtime drops to 25 minutes in tough conditions.

specs.Runtime: Up to 40 minutes (25 in tough conditions)

pros: Petrol-rivalling power in a cordless mower
Handles long, unruly grass well
Sturdy, semi-pro build quality
cons: Runtime drops significantly in tough conditions
Quick-release handle bolts can pop loose

products.name: Rotak 34R
products.best_for: Small to medium gardens that want a roller for lawn stripes
products.summary: A capable all-rounder with an integrated roller for classic lawn stripes, comfortable to push and easy to manoeuvre with one hand in Expert Reviews' tests. It tackled longer grass with ease despite modest power on paper, though the 10m cord can be limiting on longer gardens.
pros: Produces neat lawn stripes via integrated roller
Comfortable, easy to manoeuvre
Copes well with longer grass despite modest power
cons: 10m cord limits reach on larger gardens

products.name: AdvancedRotak 44-750
products.best_for: Medium to large lawns on a budget who don't mind a cable
products.summary: A powerful, fairly affordable mower that gave a fantastic clean cut on well-treated lawns while still chomping through thick, wet grass without much jamming in testing. Ergoflex handles made it comfortable on slopes and corners, and it's relatively quiet for an electric mower, though the cable requires care.
pros: Fantastic clean cut on flat, well-treated lawns
Chomps through thick, wet grass with little jamming
Relatively quiet for an electric mower
Removable, brightly coloured cable
cons: Cable limits convenience compared to cordless models

products.name: Aspire LC34-P4A
products.best_for: Buyers who want a mower that stores away neatly
products.key_spec: 18V battery, 34cm cutting width, folds for upright/wall storage
products.summary: A robust cordless mower that folds up compactly enough to hang on a shed wall, with quick lever-based cutting height adjustment. Expert Reviews found it lightweight, manoeuvrable and brilliant on small-to-medium flat lawns, though it occasionally jammed on longer, thicker clumps.
pros: Folds compactly for upright or wall storage
Lightweight and manoeuvrable
Quick, easy cutting height adjustment
Fairly quiet for a cordless mower
cons: Can occasionally jam on longer, thicker grass clumps

products.name: GC-HM30
products.best_for: Small gardens and buyers who want a cheap, fume-free mower
products.key_spec: 30cm cutting width, cylinder blade, no battery or cable required
products.summary: A cheap, no-frills, entirely manual mower that's the lightest on this list at 7.5kg, with solid build quality for the price. Expert Reviews notes it's fine for a quick trim on a cool evening, but the first cut of spring or longer grass can be genuinely hard work.
pros: Very cheap
Lightest mower on test
No fuel, battery or cable needed
Solid build quality for the price
cons: Hard, sweaty work on longer or thicker grass

products.name: Izy HRG 466 PK
products.best_for: Large or lumpy lawns needing sustained, stress-free power
products.key_spec: 145cc Honda petrol engine, 46cm cutting width, steel deck
products.summary: A rugged, long-lasting petrol mower that Expert Reviews found worked as well on lumpy lawns with longer grass as on a pancake-flat show garden. The latest engine is easier to start and more forgiving of lower-quality fuel, though it's loud at 94dB and the steel deck adds weight.
pros: Handles lumpy lawns and longer grass with ease
Rugged, long-lasting steel deck build
Large 50l grass box
Easier starting and fuel tolerance on the latest engine
cons: Heavy steel deck takes effort to manoeuvre

products.name: EasiGlide Plus 330V
products.best_for: Small gardens with sloping or uneven lawns
products.key_spec: 1,700W mains-powered, 33cm cutting width, hovers on an air cushion
products.summary: An affordable hover mower that Expert Reviews found rode smoothly on a cushion of air and dealt impressively with rough grass, overgrown sections and slopes. It doesn't give as neat a cut as a rotary mower, and changing the cutting height requires unscrewing the blade with a supplied spanner.
pros: Excellent on sloping or uneven lawns
Lightweight and easy to manoeuvre
Good value for a small garden
cons: Less neat, orderly cut than rotary mowers

guide.a: Cordless mowers offer the most convenience with no cable or fumes, but cost more upfront for the battery. Corded electric mowers are cheaper and never run out of charge mid-mow, but you're tied to a cable and socket. Petrol mowers suit large or difficult gardens where sustained power matters more than convenience or noise.

guide.q: What cutting width do I need?
guide.a: A narrower cutting width (30-35cm) suits smaller gardens and gives more manoeuvrability around borders and obstacles. A wider cut (40cm-plus) covers a large, open lawn faster but is bulkier to store and turn in tight spaces.

Rotary mowers, the most common type, give a good all-round cut on most lawns. Hover mowers glide on an air cushion, making them ideal for sloped or uneven lawns. Manual cylinder mowers need your own power but are cheap, quiet and fume-free, best suited to small, flat, regularly-mown lawns.

guide.q: How much battery runtime do I actually need?
guide.a: As a rough guide, small lawns are comfortably covered by 20-30 minutes of runtime, while larger or more demanding lawns benefit from a mower like the Ego or Stihl here with 40 minutes or more, or a spare battery to swap in partway through.
